summary: The Emeya is Lotus's electric four-door hyper-GT, and Australian reviewers agree it is a genuinely resolved luxury EV — CarExpert praises air suspension that "breathes nicely with the road" rather than feeling floaty, and CarsGuide rates the chassis agile enough to hold its own against a Porsche Taycan while offering far more rear legroom. Where they part company is on whether it is still a Lotus: at 2480-2575kg CarsGuide argues it "abandons Lotus' lightweight principles" and that the heaviness dulls its edge. The bigger buyer risk is commercial rather than dynamic — Australia bought 5 in 2024, 3 in 2025 and none year-to-date in 2026, making it the slowest-selling car you can actually walk in and order.
pros: Wheelbase is roughly 200mm longer than a Porsche Taycan's, so rear legroom is genuinely adult-sized where the Taycan and Audi e-tron GT are cramped
800V architecture charges at up to 350kW for a 10-80 per cent top-up in about 14 minutes, comfortably quicker than a Taycan on the same charger
Liftback tailgate gives 509 litres behind the rear seats and 1388 litres folded, plus a 34-litre frunk — far more usable than the sedan-booted e-tron GT
Unconditional five-year/150,000km vehicle warranty with eight years/200,000km on the battery, no dealer-servicing strings attached
Entry 600 grade is certified at 580km combined WLTP from a 98.9kWh usable pack, ahead of the 506km BMW i5 M60 at a similar price
cons: Australian volume is effectively nil — 5 sales in 2024, 3 in 2025 and zero year-to-date in 2026 — so there is almost no used-buyer base and resale risk is severe
Only five Lotus retailers nationally (Brisbane, Sydney, Melbourne, Adelaide, Perth), meaning no franchised service or warranty support outside a capital city

Documented heavy discounting: Carscoops reported in May 2026 that UK dealers were taking roughly 36 per cent off a $189K-equivalent Emeya, and the Australian entry price has already been cut from $189,990 to $177,990
Kerb weight of 2480-2575kg is close to a large SUV, and CarsGuide judges that the mass blunts the agility the badge implies
Lotus Australia publishes no prices on its website or configurator, so the grade walk above the entry 600 cannot be compared without visiting a retailer
